````math
## Appendix E Comparison with Closely Related Methods

Several recent methods address instability in on-policy distillation,
but differ from FIRE in both setting and mechanism. In particular, some
methods below study standard teacher-student on-policy distillation,
whereas FIRE targets feedback-based *self-distillation*, where the
teacher and student are derived from the same model. In this section, we
clarify in detail how FIRE differs from existing works.

##### SRPO and SCOPE.

SRPO ([Li et al., 2026a](#bib.bib1)) and SCOPE ([Zheng et al.,
2026](#bib.bib2)) also route correct and incorrect trajectories
differently. SRPO operates in a self-distillation setting, sending
correct samples to GRPO and failed samples to self-distillation. SCOPE
instead uses conventional teacher-student on-policy distillation, with
student-perplexity-weighted on-policy SFT for correct trajectories and
teacher-perplexity-weighted distillation for incorrect ones. FIRE, by
contrast, uses Fisher-informed re-weighted on-policy SFT for correct
responses and, for incorrect responses, attributes the induced gradient
to individual feedback fields. Neither method performs individual
feedback-field attribution or constrains both branches with Fisher and
gradient-derived insights.

##### DemoPSD.

DemoPSD ([Li et al., 2026b](#bib.bib3)) is also an on-policy
self-distillation method and is the closest baseline in terms of target
recalibration. It measures teacher-student disagreement using per-token
Jensen-Shannon Divergence (JSD) and geometrically shifts the privileged
teacher toward the student when disagreement is large. FIRE, by
contrast, measures the gradient induced by the feedback-conditioned
teacher. The full teacher is unchanged when its gradient lies within the
local budget, with only unsafe updates triggering feedback-field
attribution and, when still necessary, subsequent contraction.
Therefore, consideration for individual feedback field influence via
leave-one-out counterfactuals is not considered with DemoPSD.

##### Veto.

Veto ([Jang et al., 2026](#bib.bib25)) studies conventional
teacher-student on-policy distillation rather than self-distillation. It
constructs a geometric teacher-student target with a scheduled
interpolation coefficient. FIRE is instead token-specific and determined
by the attribution-aware gradient relative to a Fisher-derived radius.
FIRE also routes by correctness and attributes unsafe updates to
individual feedback fields.

##### TOP-D and TrOPD.

TOP-D ([Xie et al., 2026](#bib.bib23)) and TrOPD ([Xing et al.,
2026](#bib.bib24)) likewise address conventional on-policy distillation
with distinct teacher and student models, rather than the feedback-based
self-distillation setting. While TOP-D and TrOPD also constrain
unreliable or overly large distillation updates, their trust-region
mechanisms differ from FIRE’s Fisher-informed local gradient radius.
TOP-D constructs a proximal teacher and uses internal trust-region
iterations, while TrOPD identifies teacher-verifiable regions from
teacher-student agreement and treats outliers separately. FIRE instead
directly constrains the token-level gradient induced by a
feedback-conditioned self-teacher using the student’s local Fisher
geometry. In addition, neither TOP-D nor TrOPD routes trajectories by
correctness into separate correct and incorrect-response objectives.

##### Key distinction.

FIRE combines outcome routing, feedback-field counterfactual attribution
in gradient space, and a token-level Fisher-informed update bound. The
attribution determines *which feedback-dependent direction* to follow,
while the Fisher radius determines *how far* the update may move.
Importantly, FIRE leaves the original full-feedback target unchanged
whenever its induced update is already within this radius and
outperforms all the aforementioned baselines in Sec.
[4](#S4 "4 Experimental Results ‣ Fisher-Informed Recalibration for Feedback-Based On-Policy Self-Distillation of LLMs").

## Appendix F Additional FIRE Details

This section gives the derivations and implementation details omitted
from
Sec. [3](#S3 "3 Proposed Methodology ‣ Fisher-Informed Recalibration for Feedback-Based On-Policy Self-Distillation of LLMs").
All coefficients and target distributions are constructed from detached
model outputs. Backpropagation is performed only through the live
student distribution $`p_{\bm{\theta}}^{t}`$.

### F.1 Execution Order and Feedback Conditioning

At optimizer step $`k`$, the self-distillation process inspired
by [Hübotter et al. (2026)](#bib.bib11) performs the following
operations:

1.  1.
    Sample a prompt $`\mathbf{x}`$ and generate one response
    $`\mathbf{y}\sim\pi_{\bm{\theta}_{k}}(\cdot\mid\mathbf{x})`$ using
    the current student.
2.  2.
    Construct privileged feedback
    $`\mathbf{c}=\mathcal{F}(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y})`$ for that response.
3.  3.
    Score the fixed response with the live student conditioned on
    $`(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{y}_{<t})`$ and with the EMA teacher
    conditioned on $`(\mathbf{x},\mathbf{c},\mathbf{y}_{<t})`$.
4.  4.
    Backpropagate the reverse-KL loss and update the student.
5.  5.
    Update the EMA teacher from the newly updated student.

The teacher therefore supplies feedback-conditioned supervision on
samples visited by the student. It neither produces the training
trajectory nor receives gradients. FIRE preserves this rollout,
student-update, and EMA-update ordering, while feedback construction and
EMA-teacher scoring are performed only for incorrect responses after
outcome routing.

### F.2 Exact Reverse-KL Logit Gradient

Let $`p^{t}_{\bm{\theta}}=\operatorname{softmax}(\mathbf{z}^{t})`$ and
let $`q^{t}`$ be a detached target. The token-level reverse KL is

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathrm{KL}\!\left(p^{t}_{\bm{\theta}}\,\middle\|\,q^{t}\right)=\sum_{v}p^{t}_{\bm{\theta}}(v)\left[\log p^{t}_{\bm{\theta}}(v)-\log q^{t}(v)\right].
``` |  | (16) |

Using

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\frac{\partial p^{t}_{\bm{\theta}}(v)}{\partial z^{t}(u)}=p^{t}_{\bm{\theta}}(v)\bigl(\mathbf{1}[u=v]-p^{t}_{\bm{\theta}}(u)\bigr),
``` |  | (17) |

the logit gradient evaluated at the detached student snapshot
$`p^{t}(v)=\operatorname{sg}[p^{t}_{\bm{\theta}_{k}}(v)]`$ is

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\bigl[\mathbf{g}^{t}(q^{t})\bigr]_{v}=p^{t}(v)\left[\log\frac{p^{t}(v)}{q^{t}(v)}-\mathbb{E}_{u\sim p^{t}}\!\left[\log\frac{p^{t}(u)}{q^{t}(u)}\right]\right].
``` |  | (18) |

The expectation centers the gradient so that
$`\sum_{v}\bigl[\mathbf{g}^{t}(q^{t})\bigr]_{v}=0`$. FIRE compares
feedback fields using this gradient because it represents the update the
target would actually apply to the current student. Probability changes
in regions assigned negligible student mass have little immediate
effect, whereas smaller changes on high-mass tokens may strongly affect
training.

### F.3 Fisher Scale and Learning-Rate Calibration

For a categorical student distribution $`p^{t}`$, the softmax Fisher
matrix is

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbf{F}(p^{t})=\operatorname{diag}(p^{t})-p^{t}(p^{t})^{\top},
``` |  | (19) |

whose trace is

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\phi^{t}=\operatorname{tr}\mathbf{F}(p^{t})=1-\lVert p^{t}\rVert_{2}^{2}.
``` |  | (20) |

For an on-policy token $`y_{t}\sim p^{t}`$, the hard-label logit
gradient is $`p^{t}-\mathbf{e}_{y_{t}}`$, and, using
$`\mathbb{E}_{y_{t}\sim p^{t}}[p^{t}(y_{t})]=\lVert p^{t}\rVert_{2}^{2}`$,

|  |  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|----|
|  | $`\displaystyle\mathbb{E}_{y_{t}\sim p^{t}}\lVert p^{t}-\mathbf{e}_{y_{t}}\rVert_{2}^{2}`$ | $`\displaystyle=\mathbb{E}_{y_{t}\sim p^{t}}\left[1+\lVert p^{t}\rVert_{2}^{2}-2p^{t}(y_{t})\right]`$ |  |  |
|  |  | $`\displaystyle=1+\lVert p^{t}\rVert_{2}^{2}-2\lVert p^{t}\rVert_{2}^{2}=1-\lVert p^{t}\rVert_{2}^{2}=\phi^{t}.`$ |  | (21) |

Therefore, $`\sqrt{\phi^{t}}`$ is the root-mean-square on-policy
hard-label gradient norm. FIRE defines

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
s_{k}=\max\left(1,\frac{a_{k}}{a_{0}}\right),\qquad\rho_{k}^{t}=\frac{\sqrt{\phi^{t}}}{s_{k}}.
``` |  | (22) |

When the scheduled learning rate is at or below the hyperparameter
nominal rate value, FIRE retains the Fisher scale. When $`a_{k}>a_{0}`$,
the radius contracts inversely with the learning-rate increase. The
maximum prevents a decaying scheduler from enlarging the permitted
gradient.

### F.4 Correct-Branch Re-weighting as Gradient Projection

For a verified token, define

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbf{g}_{+}^{t}=p^{t}-\mathbf{e}_{y_{t}},\qquad\beta^{t}=\min\!\left(1,\frac{\rho_{k}^{t}}{\lVert\mathbf{g}_{+}^{t}\rVert_{2}}\right).
``` |  | (23) |

Because $`\beta^{t}`$ is detached from the computation graph,

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\nabla_{\mathbf{z}^{t}}\ell_{+}^{t}=\beta^{t}\bigl(p^{t}-\mathbf{e}_{y_{t}}\bigr).
``` |  | (24) |

Consequently,

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\left\lVert\nabla_{\mathbf{z}^{t}}\ell_{+}^{t}\right\rVert_{2}=\min\!\left(\lVert\mathbf{g}_{+}^{t}\rVert_{2},\rho_{k}^{t}\right).
``` |  | (25) |

Below the radius, FIRE is identical to ordinary on-policy SFT. Above it,
the gradient lands exactly on the boundary without changing its
direction.

We note the exact activation condition for the correct branch. Since
$`\lVert\mathbf{g}_{+}^{t}\rVert_{2}^{2}=1+\lVert p^{t}\rVert_{2}^{2}-2p^{t}(y_{t})`$,
clipping at the hyperparameter ($`s_{k}=1`$,
$`(\rho_{k}^{t})^{2}=\phi^{t}`$) occurs precisely when

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
p^{t}(y_{t})<\lVert p^{t}\rVert_{2}^{2}=\mathbb{E}_{u\sim p^{t}}\left[p^{t}(u)\right].
``` |  | (26) |

Clipping is therefore applied exactly to verified tokens that the
current student assigned below-average probability, i.e. to the tokens
carrying the largest hard-label gradient in an already correct trace.
This is intended: the radius equalizes the per-token step scale between
the two branches, so that a single surprising token inside a correct
response cannot dominate the update relative to the feedback-conditioned
branch. The cost is that the most informative correct tokens are the
ones rescaled, which trades per-token learning speed on the correct
branch for comparability of step size across branches.

### F.5 Exact Leave-One-Field-Out Influence

For field $`b_{j}`$, define the full-versus-removed log-probability
residual

|     |                                                             |     |      |
|-----|-------------------------------------------------------------|-----|------|
|     |
       ``` math
       r_{j}^{t}(v)=\log q_{-j}^{t}(v)-\log q_{\mathbf{c}}^{t}(v).
       ```                                                          |     | (27) |

Subtracting
equation [18](#A6.E18 "In F.2 Exact Reverse-KL Logit Gradient ‣ Appendix F Additional FIRE Details ‣ Fisher-Informed Recalibration for Feedback-Based On-Policy Self-Distillation of LLMs")
for the two teacher views gives

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\bigl[\mathbf{g}_{\mathbf{c}}^{t}-\mathbf{g}_{-j}^{t}\bigr](v)=p^{t}(v)\left[r_{j}^{t}(v)-\mathbb{E}_{u\sim p^{t}}\left[r_{j}^{t}(u)\right]\right].
``` |  | (28) |

Therefore,

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
E_{j}^{t}=\left\lVert\mathbf{g}_{\mathbf{c}}^{t}-\mathbf{g}_{-j}^{t}\right\rVert_{2}^{2}
``` |  | (29) |

is the exact change in the local training signal caused by removing
field $`b_{j}`$. FIRE multiplies this influence by

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\chi^{t}=\begin{cases}\displaystyle\frac{\left[E_{\mathbf{c}}^{t}-(\rho_{k}^{t})^{2}\right]_{+}}{E_{\mathbf{c}}^{t}},&E_{\mathbf{c}}^{t}>0,\\[8.0pt]
0,&E_{\mathbf{c}}^{t}=0,\end{cases}
``` |  | (30) |

where
$`E_{\mathbf{c}}^{t}=\lVert\mathbf{g}_{\mathbf{c}}^{t}\rVert_{2}^{2}`$.
This agrees with
equation [10](#S3.E10 "In Step 3: Incorrect branch training. ‣ 3.2 FIRE: Fisher-Informed Recalibration ‣ 3 Proposed Methodology ‣ Fisher-Informed Recalibration for Feedback-Based On-Policy Self-Distillation of LLMs")
in every case, and $`\chi^{t}\in[0,1)`$ since $`(\rho_{k}^{t})^{2}>0`$
whenever $`p^{t}`$ is non-deterministic. The numerator is exactly the
full teacher’s gradient energy outside the permitted energy ball. If the
complete feedback-conditioned target is already inside the ball, all
field weights vanish and the full teacher is retained.

With

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
Z^{t}=(\rho_{k}^{t})^{2}+\sum_{j}w_{j}^{t},\qquad\alpha_{0}^{t}=\frac{(\rho_{k}^{t})^{2}}{Z^{t}},\qquad\alpha_{j}^{t}=\frac{w_{j}^{t}}{Z^{t}},
``` |  | (31) |

adopting the convention $`\alpha_{0}^{t}=1`$, $`\alpha_{j}^{t}=0`$ in
the degenerate case $`Z^{t}=0`$, the attribution target is the
normalized geometric mean

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
q_{A}^{t}(v)=\frac{q_{\mathbf{c}}^{t}(v)^{\alpha_{0}^{t}}\prod_{j=1}^{B}q_{-j}^{t}(v)^{\alpha_{j}^{t}}}{\sum_{u\in\mathcal{V}}q_{\mathbf{c}}^{t}(u)^{\alpha_{0}^{t}}\prod_{j=1}^{B}q_{-j}^{t}(u)^{\alpha_{j}^{t}}}.
``` |  | (32) |

Its log probability satisfies

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\log q_{A}^{t}(v)=C^{t}+\alpha_{0}^{t}\log q_{\mathbf{c}}^{t}(v)+\sum_{j}\alpha_{j}^{t}\log q_{-j}^{t}(v),
``` |  | (33) |

where $`C^{t}`$ is constant across vocabulary elements. Since
equation [18](#A6.E18 "In F.2 Exact Reverse-KL Logit Gradient ‣ Appendix F Additional FIRE Details ‣ Fisher-Informed Recalibration for Feedback-Based On-Policy Self-Distillation of LLMs")
is affine in $`\log q`$ after centering, and since
$`\alpha_{0}^{t}+\sum_{j}\alpha_{j}^{t}=1`$,

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbf{g}^{t}(q_{A}^{t})=\alpha_{0}^{t}\mathbf{g}_{\mathbf{c}}^{t}+\sum_{j}\alpha_{j}^{t}\mathbf{g}_{-j}^{t}.
``` |  | (34) |

The geometric mean therefore converts the field-attribution coefficients
into an exact weighted average of the corresponding training signals. An
arithmetic probability mixture would not preserve this identity.

Two consequences of
equation [34](#A6.E34 "In F.5 Exact Leave-One-Field-Out Influence ‣ Appendix F Additional FIRE Details ‣ Fisher-Informed Recalibration for Feedback-Based On-Policy Self-Distillation of LLMs")
arise. Firstly, writing
$`\bm{\delta}_{j}^{t}=\mathbf{g}_{\mathbf{c}}^{t}-\mathbf{g}_{-j}^{t}`$,
the attribution step can be expressed as

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbf{g}^{t}(q_{A}^{t})=\mathbf{g}_{\mathbf{c}}^{t}-\frac{\chi^{t}}{Z^{t}}\sum_{j}\lVert\bm{\delta}_{j}^{t}\rVert_{2}^{2}\,\bm{\delta}_{j}^{t}.
``` |  | (35) |

Second, because
equation [34](#A6.E34 "In F.5 Exact Leave-One-Field-Out Influence ‣ Appendix F Additional FIRE Details ‣ Fisher-Informed Recalibration for Feedback-Based On-Policy Self-Distillation of LLMs")
is a convex combination,

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\lVert\mathbf{g}^{t}(q_{A}^{t})\rVert_{2}\leq\max\left(\lVert\mathbf{g}_{\mathbf{c}}^{t}\rVert_{2},\max_{j}\lVert\mathbf{g}_{-j}^{t}\rVert_{2}\right),
``` |  | (36) |

but
$`\lVert\mathbf{g}^{t}(q_{A}^{t})\rVert_{2}>\lVert\mathbf{g}_{\mathbf{c}}^{t}\rVert_{2}`$
is possible when some $`\bm{\delta}_{j}^{t}`$ is anti-aligned with
$`\mathbf{g}_{\mathbf{c}}^{t}`$. Attribution is therefore a reweighting
of the correction direction and carries no norm guarantee on its own.
The radius is enforced by the subsequent projection.

### F.6 Incorrect-Branch Radial Projection

Let

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbf{g}_{A}^{t}=\mathbf{g}^{t}(q_{A}^{t}),\qquad\eta^{t}=\min\left(1,\frac{\rho_{k}^{t}}{\lVert\mathbf{g}_{A}^{t}\rVert_{2}}\right),
``` |  | (37) |

with $`\eta^{t}=1`$ for a zero gradient. FIRE constructs

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
q_{\mathrm{FIRE}}^{t}(v)=\frac{p^{t}(v)^{1-\eta^{t}}q_{A}^{t}(v)^{\eta^{t}}}{\sum_{u\in\mathcal{V}}p^{t}(u)^{1-\eta^{t}}q_{A}^{t}(u)^{\eta^{t}}}.
``` |  | (38) |

Up to a vocabulary-independent normalizer $`C_{\eta}^{t}`$,

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\log q_{\mathrm{FIRE}}^{t}=(1-\eta^{t})\log p^{t}+\eta^{t}\log q_{A}^{t}+C_{\eta}^{t},
``` |  | (39) |

so the log-ratio appearing in
equation [18](#A6.E18 "In F.2 Exact Reverse-KL Logit Gradient ‣ Appendix F Additional FIRE Details ‣ Fisher-Informed Recalibration for Feedback-Based On-Policy Self-Distillation of LLMs")
reduces to

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\log p^{t}-\log q_{\mathrm{FIRE}}^{t}=\eta^{t}\left(\log p^{t}-\log q_{A}^{t}\right)-C_{\eta}^{t}.
``` |  | (40) |

The constant $`C_{\eta}^{t}`$ cancels under the centering in
equation [18](#A6.E18 "In F.2 Exact Reverse-KL Logit Gradient ‣ Appendix F Additional FIRE Details ‣ Fisher-Informed Recalibration for Feedback-Based On-Policy Self-Distillation of LLMs"),
and the remaining factor $`\eta^{t}`$ passes through linearly, yielding

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\mathbf{g}^{t}(q_{\mathrm{FIRE}}^{t})=\eta^{t}\mathbf{g}_{A}^{t}.
``` |  | (41) |

Therefore,

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\left\lVert\mathbf{g}^{t}(q_{\mathrm{FIRE}}^{t})\right\rVert_{2}=\min\!\left(\lVert\mathbf{g}_{A}^{t}\rVert_{2},\rho_{k}^{t}\right).
``` |  | (42) |

Attribution changes which feedback-dependent direction is followed, and
radial projection then restricts how strongly that direction is applied.
The two stages are sequential rather than independent, since
$`\eta^{t}`$ is determined by $`\lVert\mathbf{g}_{A}^{t}\rVert_{2}`$ and
therefore by the outcome of the attribution step.

### F.7 Unified Bound and Its Scope

Equations [25](#A6.E25 "In F.4 Correct-Branch Re-weighting as Gradient Projection ‣ Appendix F Additional FIRE Details ‣ Fisher-Informed Recalibration for Feedback-Based On-Policy Self-Distillation of LLMs")
and [42](#A6.E42 "In F.6 Incorrect-Branch Radial Projection ‣ Appendix F Additional FIRE Details ‣ Fisher-Informed Recalibration for Feedback-Based On-Policy Self-Distillation of LLMs")
imply that either routed branch satisfies

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\lVert\mathbf{g}_{\mathrm{branch}}^{t}\rVert_{2}\leq\rho_{k}^{t}=\frac{\sqrt{\phi^{t}}}{\max(1,a_{k}/a_{0})}.
``` |  | (43) |

When $`a_{k}\geq a_{0}`$,

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
a_{k}\lVert\mathbf{g}_{\mathrm{branch}}^{t}\rVert_{2}\leq a_{0}\sqrt{\phi^{t}}.
``` |  | (44) |

This is a local output-logit bound. It does not directly bound the full
parameter update, next-token KL, or global convergence, which
additionally depend on the model Jacobian, optimizer preconditioning and
momentum, gradient accumulation, and parameter-gradient clipping.

### F.8 Computation and Memory

Correct responses require one student rollout and one student scoring
pass, but no teacher evaluation. Incorrect responses use the same
rollout, one live student scoring pass, one full-feedback EMA-teacher
score, and $`B`$ leave-one-field-out teacher scores. None of the teacher
passes generates a new response.

The leave-one-field-out views can be streamed. Define

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
S_{w}^{t}=\sum_{j}w_{j}^{t},\qquad R_{w}^{t}=\sum_{j}w_{j}^{t}\left(\log q_{-j}^{t}-\log q_{\mathbf{c}}^{t}\right).
``` |  | (45) |

Then, since $`1-S_{w}^{t}/Z^{t}=(\rho_{k}^{t})^{2}/Z^{t}`$, the
attribution target can be computed as

|  |  |  |  |
|----|----|----|----|
|  |
``` math
\log q_{A}^{t}=\log\operatorname{softmax}\left(\log q_{\mathbf{c}}^{t}+\frac{R_{w}^{t}}{(\rho_{k}^{t})^{2}+S_{w}^{t}}\right).
``` |  | (46) |

The implementation therefore stores one residual accumulator rather than
all $`B`$ removed-field distributions simultaneously. FIRE introduces no
additional student rollout, student forward pass, or backward pass
beyond the underlying self-distillation loop.

Two numerical caveats apply. First, the exact gradient identities assume
full-vocabulary reverse KL, while truncating the vocabulary support
makes them approximate. Second, because
equation [32](#A6.E32 "In F.5 Exact Leave-One-Field-Out Influence ‣ Appendix F Additional FIRE Details ‣ Fisher-Informed Recalibration for Feedback-Based On-Policy Self-Distillation of LLMs")
is a geometric mean, $`\log q_{A}^{t}(v)`$ diverges whenever any teacher
view with $`\alpha_{j}^{t}>0`$ assigns vanishing mass to $`v`$, so
$`q_{A}^{t}`$ effectively inherits the narrowest support among the
active views. In practice all teacher log-probabilities are floored at a
small constant before accumulation into $`R_{w}^{t}`$, which bounds the
residual and leaves the identities in
Appendices [F.5](#A6.SS5 "F.5 Exact Leave-One-Field-Out Influence ‣ Appendix F Additional FIRE Details ‣ Fisher-Informed Recalibration for Feedback-Based On-Policy Self-Distillation of LLMs")
and [F.6](#A6.SS6 "F.6 Incorrect-Branch Radial Projection ‣ Appendix F Additional FIRE Details ‣ Fisher-Informed Recalibration for Feedback-Based On-Policy Self-Distillation of LLMs")
accurate to that floor.
````
